nodes.summary: A singleton set of vectors is linear, with no periods.
nodes.title: A singleton set of vectors is linear

nodes.summary: A set of vectors is linear when it consists of a base vector plus arbitrary nonnegative combinations of finitely many period vectors, with one coefficient per position in the period list.
nodes.title: Linear set of vectors

nodes.summary: The empty set of vectors is semilinear.
nodes.title: The empty set is semilinear

nodes.summary: A singleton set of vectors is semilinear.
nodes.title: A singleton set of vectors is semilinear

nodes.summary: A set of vectors is semilinear when it is a finite union of linear sets.
nodes.title: Semilinear set of vectors

nodes.summary: Duplicate periods get independent coefficients: with `P = [p, p]`, the coefficients `(1, 0)` give `p`.
nodes.title: Duplicate periods get independent coefficients

nodes.summary: The unguarded recursion agrees with `linComb` on equal-length inputs.
nodes.title: Unguarded linear combination agrees on equal lengths

nodes.summary: Mismatched lengths are rejected: a longer coefficient list does not silently drop coefficients.
nodes.title: Linear combination with too many coefficients is zero

nodes.summary: Mismatched lengths are rejected: a shorter coefficient list does not silently truncate.
nodes.title: Linear combination with too few coefficients is zero

nodes.summary: The linear combination of a list of period vectors with a coefficient list `c`: pair the two lists position by position and sum the scaled periods, and reject mismatched lengths by returning `0` (the length guard is checked up front, before the recursion, so a shorter coefficient list cannot silently truncate and a longer one cannot silently drop coefficients). Coefficients are indexed by *position* in `P`, not by…
nodes.title: Linear combination of period vectors

nodes.summary: The Parikh image of the empty language is empty.
nodes.title: Parikh image of the empty language is empty

nodes.summary: The Parikh image of a singleton language is the singleton of the Parikh vector.
nodes.title: Parikh image of a singleton language

nodes.summary: The Parikh image of a union is the union of the Parikh images.
nodes.title: Parikh image of a union of languages

nodes.summary: The Parikh image of a language: the set of Parikh vectors of its words.
nodes.title: Parikh image of a language

nodes.summary: The Parikh vector of the empty word is zero.
nodes.title: Parikh vector of the empty word is zero

nodes.summary: The Parikh vector of a word: the function counting, for each letter, how many times it occurs in the word.
nodes.title: Parikh vector of a word

nodes.summary: Semilinear sets are closed under union.
nodes.title: Semilinear sets are closed under union

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
